heading: INT. NORTH STAR ROLLER RINK - DJ BOOTH - NIGHT

units.text: INT. NORTH STAR ROLLER RINK - DJ BOOTH - NIGHT
A glass cubicle above an empty rink.
A mirror ball turns, throwing flecks of light.
Pink neon buzzes.
The floor below is bare maple, still scuffed from the evening's skaters.
INEZ CASTELLANOS-WHITE, sixteen, in a rental-skate shirt with her name sewn on the pocket, sits alone at the turntables.
She wears headphones around her neck.
A cassette recorder sits beside a cardboard box of tapes.
She presses PLAY.
A hiss of tape.
Okay, is it recording? It's recording. This is the first mix tape of Inez Castellanos-White, age twelve. Do not tell my brother.
units.name: INEZ

units.text: She freezes the tape with a click.
Pushes her chair back.
Stares down at the empty rink.
She laughs, short, and rubs her eyes with the heel of her hand.
Twelve.
units.name: INEZ

units.text: She presses PLAY again.
I'm going to be a DJ. I'm going to be the best one in the whole state, and when I'm famous I'm going to buy this rink and nobody will ever skate backward again.
units.name: INEZ

units.text: A hiccup of tape.
A pause.
A younger giggle.
Okay, here's my favorite song. I made the transition myself.
units.name: INEZ

units.text: A scratchy needle drop.
A bright pop song swells over the tape hiss.
Inez listens.
Her foot starts to tap.
She stops it.
Rewinds.
Plays again.
Stops.
She picks up the tape and turns it over in her fingers.
You were so bad.
units.name: INEZ

units.text: She goes to the turntables and pulls a record from its sleeve.
She sets it on the platter.
Lowers the needle.
The same bright pop song, clean and loud, fills the empty rink.
She lifts the second turntable's arm and brings it down at a point she knows by heart.
The song doubles, then slides into the next, a seam so smooth it is nearly invisible.
She watches the empty floor.
Her shoulders loosen.
There.
units.name: INEZ

units.text: She picks up the cassette recorder, presses RECORD, and holds the microphone close to her mouth.
Okay. This is the second mix tape of Inez Castellanos-White, age sixteen. It's recording.
units.name: INEZ

units.text: She laughs.
She lets the music run under it.
Do not tell my brother.
units.name: INEZ

units.text: The mirror ball turns.
Light slides across the floor, across her face, across the boxes of tapes.
On the maple below, for a moment, it looks as though someone is skating.
Inez ejects the cassette, writes on its label with a marker, and puts it in her pocket.
She turns off the neon.
The booth goes dark except for the mirror ball's last slow spin.
